title.narrative: Contribution toward achieving the targets of National Strategic Plan for Tuberculosis prevention, care and control in Pakistan

description.narrative: Pakistan - Tuberculosis - National TB Control Programme Pakistan - NTP. This program has the following goals: To reduce TB mortality rate by 40% by 2023 compared to 2015. To reduce estimated TB incidence by at least 4% in 2023 compared to 2015. The objectives of this program are: By the end of 2024, procure and install 36 PSA plants aimed at improving the country's generation of medical oxygen. By the end of 2024, procure and install 36 PSA plants aimed at improving the country's generation of medical oxygen. To detect and notify at least 1,300,000 cases of new TB episode during the years 2021 to 2023. By the end of 2025, establish 1 Centres of Excellence (CoE) in each targert district (15 in total). By the end of 2025, establish 1 Centres of Excellence (CoE) in each targert district (15 in total). To maintain the annual treatment success rate at 90% and over during the years 2021 to 2023. By the end of 2025, create awareness regarding IPC practices by conducting 9000 orientation/demonstration sessions on IPC targeting frontline health facility and community workers. By the end of 2025, create awareness regarding IPC practices by conducting 9000 orientation/demonstration sessions on IPC targeting frontline health facility and community workers. To enroll in treatment with 2nd line TB medicines 21,000 cases of MDR/RR-TB cases during the years 2021 to 2023. To ensure the provision of preventive TB therapy to at least 650,000 eligible people during the years 2021 to 2023. By the end of 2025, install 13 incinerators (4 by IHHN and 9 by NTP) in 13 districts to strengthen the hospital waste management system. By the end of 2025, install 13 incinerators (4 by IHHN and 9 by NTP) in 13 districts to strengthen the hospital waste management system. To Implement case based DHIS-2 in 1,611 TB health care facilities by the end of June 2024. To Implement case based DHIS-2 in 1,611 TB health care facilities by the end of June 2024. To provide improved WASH services in the targeted 1425 Healthcare facilities and TB clinic to reduce the vulnerability of infectious diseases by 2025. To provide improved WASH services in the targeted 1425 Healthcare facilities and TB clinic to reduce the vulnerability of infectious diseases by 2025. To enhance the capacity of 2130 Community Healthcare Workers and sanitary staff on infection prevention and control to respond the COVID19 and break the chain of infection, by 2025.. To enhance the capacity of 2130 Community Healthcare Workers and sanitary staff on infection prevention and control to respond the COVID19 and break the chain of infection, by 2025.. To enhance the capabilities of 12 Community-based organizations to respond to infectious diseases outbreaks and advocate for social accountability.
